rows.note: EXPECTED (written before the first start): the own stack of the body at the pad holds the Kerbin layers (4 of 5 built); at least 1 or the start measures nothing.

EXPECTED (written before the start, 2026-11-15): of 96 hours from the start at least one with a cover of 0.4 to 0.7 over the pad (the field's cover varies over days; K-T2 found such hours at every start).
EXPECTED: the chosen hour's cover 0.45 to 0.65 (nearest 0.55).
EXPECTED: with raytracing Full pinned the main mod's rays ask for clouds every frame (RayCloudSeam.Ask in RtKsp's cloud callback). 0 means the raytracing is off or failed to start.
EXPECTED: with rtOwnClouds off there is no pack and no texture (the setting's default is on; the probe turns it off for the A/B base).
EXPECTED: with the pack standing the atmospheres publish the view for the pad's body every frame (RayCloudSeam.Fresh).
EXPECTED: the main mod puts the own layers into its traced frames instead of EVE's (RtOwnCloudBlock.Fill true within the last 2 frames).
EXPECTED: the proxy's status names no problem with input 7 (a texture it cannot share drops every traced frame; found in the RT player with R32G32_FLOAT, fixed by RGBA32F).

EXPECTED (written before start 65): the proxy's own status line carries cloudsMode=2 for its latest traced frame, so the dxgi.dll in the game is a build that reads the own cloud block. 0 means a dxgi.dll from before this build (it would read the block as EVE's layer and every other row would still pass).

EXPECTED: the vessel's place in the view's map frame (WorldToMap of the published view applied to the vessel's position from the body's centre) comes out at the vessel's latitude and longitude within 0.05 degrees. A wrong frame (a mirrored axis, a rotation of the body missing from the matrix) is off by degrees: this is the row that catches it; the scan below is frame-free.
EXPECTED: the view's lowest base and highest top (m from the centre) are the pack entries'.
EXPECTED: the view's width, slice height, layer count and body are the pack's.
EXPECTED: the radius in the header row is the body's radius.
INFORMATION: of the 96 hours those with precipitation over the vessel (level above 0.02); the probe never chooses one, so no rain deck lies under the layers in the pictures.

EXPECTED (written before start 65): the largest mean colour difference (0 to 1, every fifth texel) between an on and an off picture of the same view is at least 0.001; clouds move and the sun drifts between the two, so the number is an upper bound of the rays' part. 0 or less means no view changed: the own clouds are not in the rays' result or not in view.
INFORMATION: on against off, the flight camera as the start has it. -1 means a picture could not be read.
INFORMATION: on against off, camera level at the start's heading.
INFORMATION: on against off, camera level, a quarter turn from the start's heading.
INFORMATION: on against off, camera level, a half turn from the start's heading.
INFORMATION: on against off, camera level, three quarter turns from the start's heading.

The cost figures below are a result only where this is 1: every window of the interleaved cost measurement did what its kind says (pack taken by the rays, or hidden from them) and no one of the five rounds of a kind lies more than max(2 ms, 5 %) from the kind's median. A window is 30 settling frames and 60 timed frames, its figure the median frame time; the cost is the median over the rounds of (taps8 - hidden) of the same round. A valid measurement needs a quiet machine: no other process on the GPU (a Unity job or a second game moves the windows by several ms) and the rays following the switch. 0 means it was not: the figures are then not to be used.
The largest distance of a round's window figure (median frame time) from the median of its kind, over the four kinds: the noise of the cost figure. Above 2 ms the figure is not valid.
INFORMATION: the longest single frame of all cost windows (a stall of the machine, not of the layers; the windows' medians ignore it).
Windows in which the rays did not do what their kind says (the pack taken in a hidden window, or not taken in a window that shows it).

Brief acceptance: frame time of the same traced scene with the own layers in the rays (rt.rayTaps 8) against the pack kept but hidden from the rays (RtOwnClouds.HideFromRays), the median over five rounds of the pair of adjacent windows (60 timed frames each, median frame time), A4500 Medium 1707x960. EXPECTED: 0.1 to 0.5 ms (per light ray up to 4 layers x 8 taps of one filtered read). Valid only with T18.rt_cost_valid = 1. A value above 1 ms is a defect to report.

Reusable cost figure (RTSAVE): the median CPU frame time of the hidden windows: raytracing Full, the own pack standing and kept current but not in the rays; the same pose, clock and frame as the next rows.
The same scene with the pack in the rays, rt.rayTaps 8 (the default).
As rt_ms_taps8 with rt.rayTaps 4.
As rt_ms_taps8 with rt.rayTaps 16.
rt_ms_taps4 minus rt_ms_off. EXPECTED: below rt_frame_ms_delta (fewer lookups per ray).
rt_ms_taps16 minus rt_ms_off. EXPECTED: above rt_frame_ms_delta (more lookups per ray).

From the switch to the first pack. EXPECTED: 5 to 20 s: the first bake runs at 6 ms a frame (rt.firstBakeBudgetMs) and costs 150 to 500 ms of the main thread, 30 to 100 frames of a traced scene. Start 65 measured 182 s at the former 0.25 ms a frame, which made the probe run past its 10 minutes.

EXPECTED: the main-thread time of one whole bake 150 to 500 ms (offline, Debug, four layers: 170 ms without and 520 ms with height variation at stride 2). Limit 800 ms (start 65: 1475 ms before the baker's near check and column loop were made cheap).
INFORMATION: real time from the start of the first bake to its pack (the pack's age when it stands).

The worst tick of the first bake (budget 6 ms plus the check interval of 64 texels, the first tick carries the JIT and the 4 MB allocation). The first bake happens once, when the switch goes on; the refresh ticks are T18.refresh_tick_worst_ms.
The worst tick of the bakes that keep a standing pack current (budget 0.3 ms plus the check interval of 64 texels). A tick above 2 ms is a hitch the refresh adds to a traced frame.

The main-thread time baking took per frame over the interleaved cost windows (about 1400 frames, the bake's own stopwatch): the cost of keeping the pack current. EXPECTED 0.2 to 0.3 (budget 0.3 ms a frame, the owner's limit for the own layers in the rays: 0.3 ms).
INFORMATION: uploads of the whole pack texture during the cost windows (one per finished refresh bake; the live fields go by a one-row copy).

[proposed] The largest age of the sky the standing pack shows (time since its bake began) over one whole refresh cycle. EXPECTED 20 to 80 s: the bake's main-thread time over the 0.3 ms a frame, in frames of a traced scene (40 to 60 ms). Start 65 had a pack 180 to 360 s behind the sky (continuous rebake at 0.25 ms). A bound that rises means the bake got dearer or the frames faster.
INFORMATION: real time of the last refresh bake from its start to its pack.
INFORMATION: main-thread time of the last refresh bake.
INFORMATION: the age of the standing pack at the moment of the agreement scans.
EXPECTED: at least the first bake is done when the first pack stands.

The first upload, which creates the 8 MB texture: the pack's data is copied as one block into the texture's CPU copy (no loop over the texels), then Apply. EXPECTED: 2 to 6 ms (start 66 with the per-texel expansion: 11.9 ms). Limit 8 ms.

The worst main-thread step of a refresh upload, which copies one layer slice (2 MB) a frame through a staging texture and a GPU copy: no frame uploads more than a quarter of the pack. EXPECTED: 0.5 to 2 ms. Limit 4 ms.
EXPECTED: every layer of the stack (up to 4) is in the pack. Brief: all layers.
EXPECTED: equal to the stack's layers, at most 4.
EXPECTED: 2 MB a layer at 512 x 256 on the graphics card (four floats a texel, the proxy cannot share two; 8 MB for four layers).
EXPECTED: the texture is Width x (Height x layers + 1 header row).

EXPECTED: all five kinds of place exist in the sky of the start (the start must hold a broken field and a deck with an edge near the vessel; a clear sky fails this row by name, it does not pass vacuously).

Brief acceptance: the sun's transmittance T by ray (the pack's law) against the cloud shadow field at 64 steps a span, |T_ray - T_field| of at most 0.05 (10 percent of a half-dark ground), p1 under a broken field, sun 45 degrees, the pack that stands. EXPECTED: 0 to 0.03 (offline 0.0 to 0.03 on Kerbin's four real layers).
p2 at an edge. EXPECTED: 0 to 0.05.
p3 under a deck. EXPECTED: 0 to 0.03.
p4 behind a layer pair. EXPECTED: 0 to 0.05.

p5 at the terminator (sun 6 degrees), |dT|. At a grazing sun the shell's chord averages a column over many texels and the slab model is coarse (offline p90 0.17 to 0.31 over the lattice, worst up to 0.9 over a sky with the height variation): informational, not a pass criterion.
p1 as above for a pack baked in the very call that reads the stack (no age): the model alone. If this passes and shadow_diff_p1 does not, the standing pack is stale.
p2 with the fresh pack.
p3 with the fresh pack.
p4 with the fresh pack.
p5 with the fresh pack: informational (grazing sun).
INFORMATION: |T| of the shadow pass's own field at 8 steps a span against its 64-step value: the reference of the raster side is itself coarse with the height variation on; not a pass criterion.
EXPECTED: at least 20 places of the 41 x 41 lattice (+-4 degrees, step 0.2) where the field or the ray is neither fully clear nor fully dark (T between 0.02 and 0.98).

[proposed] 90th percentile of |T_ray - T_field| over the lattice, sun 45 degrees, the pack that stands. T is the share of the sun's light, so 0.09 is a ground 9 percent of full sunlight too dark or too light at the worst tenth of the places that are not clear or dark in both. Offline on Kerbin's four real layers (soft density, types, height variation) the p90 is 0.02 to 0.08; a relative figure is not used (it is large and invisible where T is near 0).

[proposed] worst place of the lattice, sun 45 degrees, |dT|. Offline 0.14 to 0.19 on smooth maps; on maps with fine cells (two to four texels, neighbouring texels of very different type, where the pack's band and column depth are blended per texel and the field's from the blended type) up to 0.45. Start 66, before the column depth cap and the cloud band were fixed: 0.98. The scan45_worst_place_* lines of the start show, per layer, what both sides read at the three worst places.

The median of tau_ray over tau_field (tau = -ln T) at the places with T between 0.1 and 0.9, sun 45 degrees. EXPECTED 0.95 to 1.05 (offline 0.95 to 1.04). A factor of two in a layer's depth (a layer twice, not at all, a scale error) or a wrong frame moves it to 2 or 0.5; the slab model does not.
As scan45_p90 for a pack baked in the call that reads the stack: the model alone, without the age of the standing pack.
As scan45_worst for the fresh pack.
As scan45_tau_ratio for the fresh pack.

Sun 6 degrees (the chord is long), p90 |dT|. Informational: offline p90 0.15 to 0.31 without and up to 0.6 with the height variation (a shell several times the cloud's thickness: the chord crosses many texels). It is a limit of the slab-in-shell model, not of the bake.
Sun 6 degrees, worst place. Informational (offline up to 0.92).
As scan6_p90 for the fresh pack.
EXPECTED: with rtOwnCloudsLayerCap 2 the pack holds the two lowest layers (the stack's, if it has one).
EXPECTED: the switch off frees the pack, the texture and the rays' view (the rays go back to EVE's layer or none).
